## About

Inga Draper is a REALTOR® with eXp Realty based in the Charlotte, North Carolina metro
area. Her practice covers residential purchases and sales, out-of-state relocation, and
property strategy for owners deciding whether to sell, hold, or rent. She is licensed in
both North Carolina and South Carolina and publishes local market commentary on YouTube
as "Inga in the QC".

## Answers

Each page below answers one specific question directly.

- [Can I run a short-term rental in the Charlotte area?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/short-term-rental-rules-charlotte-area/): Permission is set by three independent layers — municipal zoning, HOA covenants, and insurance. Any one can prohibit it.
- [What should I know before relocating to Charlotte?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/relocating-to-charlotte/): Choose commute tolerance before neighborhood; verify school assignment at the parcel level.
- [What does a first-time buyer need to know in Charlotte?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/first-time-home-buyer-charlotte/): North Carolina's due diligence fee is generally non-refundable and must be budgeted as money at risk.
- [Should I sell, hold, or rent out my Charlotte property?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/sell-hold-or-rent-charlotte-property/): Decide on timeline and the capital gains exclusion clock, not current rent estimates.
- [What should I check before buying an investment property near Lake Norman?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/buying-investment-property-lake-norman/): Verify covenant minimum lease terms before evaluating returns.
- [How do Charlotte-area towns compare for buyers?](https://ingadraper.com/answers/charlotte-area-neighborhood-comparison/): Each town trades commute, space, walkability, or inventory. Pick the tradeoff first.
